motivation: Colony-code extinction order is size-selective but does not exceed a proportional zero-boundary null. The next independent biological question is whether the already-established within-island concentration trajectory is accompanied by a change in island-level breeding success.

source_and_aggregation.season: January chick census belongs to the breeding season beginning in the previous calendar year.
source_and_aggregation.adult_island_total: sum November breeding-pair counts across all reported colony codes within island-year
source_and_aggregation.chick_island_total: sum January num_chicks across all reported colony codes within island-season; do not use the chick dataset's colony-level num_breeding_pairs field as a denominator
source_and_aggregation.effective_colony_number: 1 / sum((colony_count / adult_island_total)^2) across strictly positive colony-code counts
source_and_aggregation.biological_range_check: require 0 <= breeding_success <= 2 for every included island-season; fail closed otherwise

primary_scope.reason: These are the stable-roster islands used in the preregistered breeding-patch concentration result. CHR and TOR have colony-code roster changes and are excluded from primary inference.
primary_scope.time: all joined positive-adult island-seasons available from 1991-2017; LIT contributes only while adult total is positive

primary_model.response: island breeding_success in chicks per breeding pair
primary_model.target: coefficient beta_neff on standardized log effective-colony number
primary_model.estimation: OLS using Frisch-Waugh-Lovell residualization against abundance control plus island and year fixed effects

inference.null: After residualizing breeding success and concentration against abundance, island and year effects, their within-island temporal alignment is exchangeable up to circular time shifts.
inference.permutation: Independently circular-shift the reduced-model breeding-success residual series within each focal island, preserving each island's residual distribution and serial ordering, then recompute beta using the frozen residualized concentration predictor.
inference.test: two-sided Monte Carlo p based on absolute beta, with +1 correction

directional_interpretation.beta_positive: Higher effective colony number predicts higher breeding success; therefore increasing concentration (lower Neff) is associated with reproductive deterioration.
directional_interpretation.beta_negative: Higher effective colony number predicts lower breeding success; therefore increasing concentration is associated with maintained or improved breeding success, consistent with selective retreat toward better-performing breeding space.
directional_interpretation.non_confirmatory: Do not choose between reproductive deterioration and selective-retreat explanations from this endpoint.

sensitivities.first_difference: Regress annual change in breeding success on annual change in log Neff and annual change in log1p abundance, after removing shared end-year means; report the Neff-change coefficient.
sensitivities.cor_hum_only: Repeat the primary two-way fixed-effect coefficient using only COR and HUM, which remain extant through 2017.
sensitivities.all_five_descriptive: Report the same coefficient for all five islands as descriptive only because CHR and TOR have colony-code roster changes.
sensitivities.success_denominator_check: Report island-season breeding-success ranges and confirm zero 0-2 cap violations.

interpretation_boundaries: This is an association between within-island spatial-demographic concentration and breeding success, not proof that concentration causes breeding success.
Year fixed effects absorb shared regional breeding-season conditions; island fixed effects absorb persistent island differences.
Controlling adult abundance separates concentration from the simple effect of population size but does not remove all time-varying habitat confounding.
Do not use colony-level chicks-per-pair for primary inference without a validated colony-code denominator crosswalk.
Do not interpret a null result as proof that breeding success is constant; it means concentration does not explain additional island-year variation under the frozen model.
